raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

When a KV connector reports a non-block-aligned prefix hit for DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded replay, the scheduler rounds it down to a whole block before applying the replay window. With a 64-token block, a 128-token replay window, and an 8,439-token remote hit, this reduces the adopted hit to 8,384 tokens, moves the replay start from 8,311 to 8,256, and can make the Decode block range disagree with the Prefill block range.

The rounding introduced in #56227 protects the SWA block containing the first replay token. This PR instead ensures generated bounded-replay SWA cache specs retain that boundary block, then preserves the exact connector hit only when every replay-enabled group has this guarantee. Direct or legacy configs without the guarantee keep the existing rounding fallback. The attention window is unchanged.

## Relationship to other work

This fixes a mainline scheduler/cache-config interaction from #56227 and does not depend on #58132. It is distinct from #57613's sparse local prefix-cache retention, #56709's native-offloading coverage for already configured `extra_retained_tokens`, and #58289's NIXL-specific source-block alignment. This PR does not claim to fix every connector's legacy block-mapping behavior.

## Test Plan & Test Result

### Environment and scope

- Model and hardware: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8 × H20 Prefill and 8 × H20 Decode; the router ran with Decode.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19`; the candidate additionally applied this PR at `88367fbc319683a8a1f6ad6b795af7326cd17f6e`.

Serving tests used Mooncake. I reviewed the corresponding NIXL hit and block-pairing code, but did not run NIXL transport or NIXL serving tests for this PR; I can add that validation if reviewers need it.

The unmodified nightly encountered an unrelated Mooncake release-only-pull issue before the target test: `MooncakeConnectorWorker.process_pulling_result` could report receive completion for a pull with no local destination blocks, although Decode had not entered `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, triggering a scheduler request-ID assertion. We applied the same temporary guard to both arms so testing could proceed: report receive completion only when `pull_tasks_count == 0 and any(local_block_ids)`. This guard is not part of this PR; the only A/B code difference was the PR.

### Single-request end-to-end check

The same 8,439-token ID sequence was sent to both arms with Decode's local prefix cache reset, a fixed seed, and exactly 1,500 generated tokens.

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| External KV hit | 8,384 | 8,439 |
| Replay start / prompt rows (derived from the hit) | 8,256 / 183 | 8,311 / 128 |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | 2.1398 | 2.3675 |
| Generation time | 7,809.51 ms | 6,610.95 ms |

### Aligned and non-aligned boundary benchmark

These are the essential serving arguments; cluster-specific network settings were identical across arms.

```bash
# Prefill
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len auto --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enable-cumem-allocator --block-size 64 --swa-bounded-replay --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","enforce_handshake_compat":false}}' --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
# Decode
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8999 vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len auto --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enable-cumem-allocator --block-size 64 --swa-bounded-replay --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","enforce_handshake_compat":false}}' --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' --enable-expert-parallel --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' --enable-per-request-metrics --per-request-spec-decode-metrics summary
```

We ran `vllm bench serve` with `prefix_repetition`, 80 measured requests per input length, 16 concurrent requests, fixed 512-token outputs, temperature 0, seed 1104, and separate warmup and P/D cache resets for each tier. The representative measured command below uses a 936-token prefix and a 64-token suffix for the 1,000-token tier; the other tiers used prefix lengths 960, 986, 1,023, and 1,024.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://192.168.1.220:30000 --model /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash --tokenizer /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 5 --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 936 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 64 --prefix-repetition-output-len 512 --num-prompts 80 --num-warmups 0 --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf --seed 1104 --temperature 0 --ignore-eos --disable-shuffle
```

`Aligned` means the actual tokenized input length is divisible by the 64-token KV block size; 1,024 and 1,088 were the intended aligned controls.

| Requested input tokens | Output tok/s, baseline → PR | DSpark mean acceptance, baseline → PR | Mean TPOT, baseline → PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 1,297.9 → 1,645.7 (+26.8%) | 3.169 → 4.552 | 10.213 → 7.369 ms |
| 1,024 (aligned) | 1,815.2 → 1,798.8 (−0.9%) | 5.133 → 5.132 | 6.655 → 6.928 ms |
| 1,050 | 1,462.4 → 1,678.1 (+14.8%) | 3.750 → 4.810 | 9.025 → 7.340 ms |
| 1,087 | 1,292.6 → 1,718.6 (+33.0%) | 3.002 → 4.721 | 10.569 → 7.215 ms |
| 1,088 (aligned) | 1,754.8 → 1,730.9 (−1.4%) | 5.026 → 4.728 | 7.188 → 7.458 ms |

All 400 measured requests per arm completed with exactly 512 output tokens. The baseline's lost external-hit tokens matched the sum of actual input lengths modulo 64, while the candidate lost none; one nominally aligned 1,088-token request tokenized to 1,089. Mean TTFT in the non-aligned group rose 14.4% under this saturated workload, so the demonstrated performance gain is in Decode TPOT and output throughput.

### Accuracy: full GSM8K A/B

EvalScope ran the complete 1,319-sample GSM8K test split at 0-shot with `temperature=0.2`, `top_p=0.95`, `seed=42`, and `reasoning_effort=high`. Baseline scored **1,269/1,319 (96.209%)**; this PR scored **1,268/1,319 (96.133%)**, a difference of −0.076 percentage points. Both arms completed every request, with no statistically distinguishable accuracy regression in this run. Their generated output-token totals differed, so this evaluation is not used for a throughput claim.
